text:
When a container restart or another environment stop cuts off a job, put its retry back in the queue with the original item's priority. Place it ahead of any not-yet-started item with equal or lower priority. Allow a priority change on any item that is not currently running, including items marked dispatched. Acceptance: (1) a test cuts off an urgent job while older normal items are queued, and the drain and the plan both pick the retry first; (2) a test shows that raising the priority of a dispatched but cut-off item succeeds and moves it in the plan; (3) the plan output shows each item's priority and whether it is resumed work; (4) the order of items that were never cut off is unchanged.

Acceptance:
- The change is made as described: A job cut off by a container restart comes back without its original priority, and its priority cannot be raised, so urgent work waits behind old normal items
- No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass
- fmt, clippy and test pass
